close_reason: Delivered in PR #272 (audited 2026-09-06: non_monotonic_commit_version exit incl. equal version; 3 tests; stacked on #262, no CI run)
description:
IndexManager.apply_transaction/3 prepends {commit_version, ...} to index_manager.versions and sets current_version: commit_version unconditionally. Nothing checks that the version advances.

A re-delivered or out-of-order transaction would therefore push a non-monotonic entry onto a list every other function treats as descending (rollback_to/2, page_for_key/3 and friends compare against it), regress current_version backwards, and double-count keys_added/keys_removed in n_keys.

Nothing can currently produce such a delivery, so this is latent rather than live. It is worth a guard as defence in depth: the failure is silent index corruption rather than a crash, which is the worst shape for it to take.

Stacked on #262.

title: IndexManager.apply_transaction/3 accepts non-monotonic versions
